title: Finite-ring vector-bundle orientation restricted to the zero section
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\geq1$ with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be Noetherian with $N$ invertible on $S$. Work in the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse images. For every compactifiable structural map $b$ write $\omega_b=b^\times A$ using the right adjoint of $Rb_!$. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes d}$, with $A_T(0)=A_T$.
Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$, with zero section $z$. Assume $\pi$ is compactifiable. For every affine trivializing open $T\subseteq S$ and linear frame $\phi:E_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_T$ over $T$, let
$$o_\phi:z_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(d)[2d]$$
be the section restriction of the inverse of the adjoint $\alpha_{p_d}:A_{\mathbf A^d_T}(d)[2d]\to\omega_{p_d}$ of the Kummer-normalized coordinate-tower counit, transported through $\phi$ by the counit-preserving comparison of compact-support right adjoints. For every overlap and every invertible linear change of frames these $o_\phi$ agree under the canonical restriction maps. They glue to a unique isomorphism
$$o_E:z^*\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S(d)[2d]$$
with these frame restrictions. It is preserved by every $S$-linear bundle isomorphism, using the counit-preserving comparison on the source. For $d=0$, $o_E$ is the identity under $E\cong S$. Empty bases and $A=0$ are allowed.
If $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$, $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$, let $\gamma_{\pi,A_S}:A_E(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^\times A_S$ be the purity map adjoint to vector-bundle integration and the canonical projection formula. Then
$$o_E=z^*(\gamma_{\pi,A_S}^{-1})$$
under the canonical ordinary-etale Tate coefficient identifications.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-sbc-affine-space], [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], [def-amb-vector-integration].

proof.text: Use the finite-coefficient projection formula and vectorIntegrationMate_isIso at A_S, as packaged in [lem-trf-bundle-section-purity-unit-isIso], to construct the actual invertible unit purity map. Pull it back by zero and precompose with inverse coefficient comparison. Its canonical inverse is an isomorphism o with the required direction.

Apply [lem-trf-bundle-section-purity-unit-normalization] to this explicitly constructed o and projection inverse p; its inverse equation is reflexive. This proves the frame normalization. For any two normalized isomorphisms choose normalized t,D by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], compare their inverse maps in every affine frame, and apply [lem-trf-bundle-section-orientation-map-ext]. Equality of inverse maps implies equality of isomorphisms.

For every frame f of M, linearity supplies a frame f' of P whose chart equals the composite chart with h. The Cartesian lifting uniqueness identifies their chart zero sections. Apply the generic section-comparison isomorphism pasting equation. The two given inverse-map normalization equations now have identical right-hand sides. The affine-frame equality detector makes o'.inv followed by the h comparison equal to o.inv. Precompose the desired forward-map equality by o'.inv and cancel using both inverse identities.

Use VectorTraceGeometry.zero_isIso to form e=asIso π. Since zπ=1, cancellation gives e.inv=z. The exceptional base-change comparison is invertible because its base map is identity, hence open; pullback and the conjugate identity comparison preserve invertibility. Its canonical asIso c is normalized by the rank-zero one-frame identity-counit equation. Apply normalized-orientation uniqueness to o and c, then take hom maps. Geometry, inverse identities and local normalization all include the empty and zero-coefficient cases.

For valuation coefficients apply exactly the same finite-ring unit-mate construction at the stated N. Its inverse orientation is normalized by [lem-trf-bundle-section-purity-unit-normalization], so inverse-map equality detection identifies it with the given normalized o. The projection inverse p and the resulting equality are precisely BundleSectionPurityCompatibility. This works for every stated annihilator N directly; no change of annihilator or choice of arithmetic purity isomorphism is needed.
